discussion_comments.comment_body: Added to `core-events.test.ts`, folded into "report discarded pending prompts": a shape test (`capture` called once with the catalog event name and exactly `{ sessionId, count, reason }`, `captureRequired` never called) and a `capturePendingPromptsDiscarded never invokes captureRequired` case in the "telemetry policy: helpers respect telemetry opt-out" block, using the disabled-adapter `TelemetryService` like the other helpers there.

Leaving this out on purpose. Counting spawns in a unit test would mean mocking `node:child_process`, which breaks the promisified `execFile` (`.child` / `{ stdout }`), or putting a shell-script `git` wrapper on PATH, which won't work on Windows. We try not to add test-only plumbing like that. The process counts were checked against real checkpoints instead: CLI and VS Code sessions on a repo with 3,000 untracked files. main peaked at 3,051 concurrent git processes and 3,046 zombies for one comparison; this branch uses 6 git processes in total per comparison. The existing tests still cover correctness for both the tracked and the third-parent lookups.

I checked that hardcoding `"skills@latest"` back into the constant makes it fail. The call-site tests keep using the constant, as you suggested.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Valid. `transcription.test.ts` mocks `@ai-sdk/openai`, so this hand-off had never run against the real adapter. The new `transcription.openai.wire.test.ts` drives `transcribeAudio` with an `openai-native` config through the real adapter and a stubbed fetch, and asserts the request reaches `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and the transcript comes back. It fails if the stubbed fetch isn't wired through. The `image_generation` model tool, which goes through the same kind of cast in the OpenAI vendor, is now covered in the wire test next to `web_search`.

Not adding tests here. This PR is one log call on the existing socket close path (the connection.closed line you mention was in an earlier revision and is gone). Asserting on the shape of an info log line would mean enabling hub logging in vitest and spying on console output to lock down field names, which is more harness than the change is worth and would make future edits to the log payload churn tests for no behavioral gain. The close path itself is already exercised by the existing server tests, which is what would catch a real regression.

agent feedback: The first three recovery tests cover the feature's main promises well: successful retry, truncation again, and nothing to compact. The tests from here onward mostly protect detailed telemetry behavior for listener errors, hooks, empty responses, and tool-call variants that the run loop already owns. If the telemetry contract is simplified to whether compaction/retry completed, I think these extra cases and much of their supporting implementation can be removed while preserving the important behavioral coverage.
